title: Tiered value language and discount guardrails
summary: Practical draft for positioning token-first pricing inside tiered offers, sample customer-facing language, competitive callouts, and enforceable discount/approval guardrails for sales. Focus: align unit metric to customer value, preserve unit economics, and make discounts predictable and auditable.
body:
Purpose:
This note creates a compact playbook for communicating why we price by tokens, how to frame tiers around customer value and operational predictability, and what discount guardrails sales should follow. Intended audience: GTM (growth + enterprise sales), solutions engineering, product marketing, and pricing ops.

Context and thesis:
- Our core value is predictable, cost-efficient LLM inference at scale. Tokens are the clearest proxy of downstream compute and therefore unit cost. Token pricing gives transparent alignment between customer usage and cost of service.
- Customers care about two things: predictable per-unit economics (to budget) and headroom (to burst). Tiers are about predictability + volume economics; reserved/committed capacity is for throughput SLAs.

High-level positioning (one-liners to use in pitch):
- For product teams: "Pay for the compute you use — tokens measure work, not seats — so you scale cost with real usage and keep tight control over unit economics."
- For finance/security/enterprise buyers: "Token-based tiers let you forecast spend against traffic while our Dedicated/Private options lock in latency and data protections."

Metric framing: why tokens (short bullets sales can memorize)
- Tokens map to inference compute: straightforward cost signal for customers and accounting internally.
- Easy to simulate and convert from test prompts (so customers can model expected bills).
- Enables fair billing across different application patterns (short conversational vs. long-document generation).
- Natural to combine with quality tiers (e.g., model variants, quantization) — same unit across model choices.

Hybrid offers and packaging guidance
- Public/Starter Tier (Self-serve): tokens-only, metered. Low friction, advertised unit price, first 100k tokens free trial.
- Growth Tier (SMB / Scale-ups): token metered + soft commit (monthly discounted unit price after threshold). Encourages customers to grow with predictable step pricing.
- Enterprise Reserved (Dedicated/Dedicated+Private): committed token minutes per month or committed throughput (tokens/sec) with steeper unit discount and SLA. Bundle options: SLOs, retention, support.
- Hybrid: for customers with predictable peak throughput, offer a committed baseline (tokens/month at discount) + overage metered at a clearly higher unit price. This preserves economics while offering predictability.

Suggested tier thresholds (examples for sales to start with; these are starting defaults to A/B test):
- Starter: 0–5M tokens/month (self-serve)
- Growth: 5M–50M tokens/month (discount starts at 10% above baseline)
- Scale: 50M–500M tokens/month (tier pricing with 15–30% discount band)
- Enterprise/Committed: 500M+ tokens/month or bespoke capacity commitments (40–60% discount band depending on commit duration and add-ons)

Discount guardrails (enforceable rules)
- MSRP unit price is the list token price for the Starter tier. All discounts must be anchored to that.
- Discount bands by commitment: up to 15% — AE discretion; 16–30% — Director approval; 31–50% — VP of Sales approval + margin check by RevOps; >50% — CFO approval and legal review.
- Discounts tied to contract terms: longer contractual commitments (12, 24, 36 months) increase allowable discounts by band (e.g., +5% per additional year up to a cap).
- No discounts on overage unit price for hybrid offers unless explicitly negotiated for a multi-year commit.
- Hardware/throughput SLAs and Private deployment add-on charges are additive and negotiable but should not be bundled into token discount calculations.

Revenue & unit-economics guardrails (for Sales Ops / Pricing Ops reference)
- Minimum gross margin target per tier: Starter 65%+, Growth 55%+, Scale 45%+, Enterprise floor 35% (these targets reflect host costs + infra amortization). All discount approvals must reference margin impact.
- If a proposed deal lowers expected margin below the floor for the tier, require an offset (e.g., multi-year commitment, non-refundable setup fee, or higher overage rate).

Competitor positioning (high-level notes to use in battlecards)
- Competitor A (closed API vendor): typically charges per request/endpoint with opaque per-request weights. Our angle: tokens are transparent and easier to forecast across prompt variations. Use: "We give you a concrete, model-agnostic unit you can simulate."
- Competitor B (cloud-managed endpoints): may offer lower list prices but complex add-ons and egress. Our angle: predictable all-inference unit economics + optional Dedicated for throughput SLAs.
- Competitor C (open-source self-host runtimes): lower per-unit baseline but hidden ops cost and scaling pain. Our angle: tradeoff analysis — we save teams engineering time and risk, and our committed tiers further reduce unit cost without building infra.

Customer-facing language snippets (web marketing + sales)
- Web short: "Token-based pricing: predictable unit economics for every prompt type. Start free, scale with usage, and reserve capacity when you need guaranteed latency."
- Sales email opener: "Hi [Name] — our token-first pricing lets you model monthly spend from a representative test prompt in minutes. If you expect bursts, our hybrid commit gives you lower per-token rates plus guaranteed throughput."
- Proposal blurb for enterprise: "Your committed tier secures a discounted unit rate and priority capacity; overages are billed at a known incremental rate so there are no surprises."

Objection handling (concise talking points)
- "Tokens are confusing": "We map tokens to a sample prompt and show expected monthly bill under multiple traffic shapes — customers can run a model on a 1k prompt and see the projected bill automatically."
- "What about different model qualities?": "Same token counts apply; different model variants have published performance profiles and suggested quantization — we recommend the model variant that balances cost and quality for your use case and show the delta."
- "We prefer seats or per-user metrics": "Seats work for admin access; tokens capture actual workload. For seat-centric billing (e.g., internal tools), we can combine a seat fee + token pool for a hybrid package."

Sales play checklist (before discount request)
- Document customer's expected token volume projection and show modeled bill for three traffic scenarios (baseline, 2x, peak).
- Identify whether the ask is for predictable cost or SLA throughput (reserve vs. discount).
- Propose one of the standard hybrid templates (commit + overage) and the default discounts.
- If customer asks for an ad-hoc discount, use the approval matrix and attach margin impact analysis.

Examples: two canned offers (copy/paste)
- Growth bundle (email copy): "Growth bundle: 12-month commit of 60M tokens/mo at $X/token (15% off list) + priority onboarding. Overage at $Y/token. This gives predictable monthly spend and a pathway to Dedicated when you need SLOs."
- Enterprise reserved example (proposal language): "We will reserve compute capacity to support up to 1B tokens/month at a committed unit rate of $Z/token (40% off list). Included: 24/7 priority support, 99.9% inference uptime SLA, and quarterly model tuning reviews."

Operational notes for commercial systems
- Ensure billing can show line-level: base commit, overage tokens, model variant surcharges, and add-on charges for Dedicated/Private. Transparency reduces disputes.
- Tag deals with discount reasons (volume, term length, strategic pilot) in CRM to inform future pricing science.

A/B experiments & next steps (what to test Q2–Q3)
- Test alternate thresholds for Growth and Scale tiers (e.g., start Growth at 2M vs 5M) to see conversion lift on self-serve -> paid.
- Run price-sensitivity tests on the advertised unit price for Starter (e.g., 0%, 10% off list on the website) to measure ACV effects.
- Measure churn by discounted deals vs. non-discounted, and track net revenue retention adjustments for discount-heavy cohorts.

Appendix: short approval matrix (quick reference)
- AE-level: approve discounts up to 15%
- Sales Director: approve 16–30% (must include margin calc)
- VP Sales + RevOps: 31–50% (deal desk review)
- CFO + Legal: >50% or unusual contractual terms (IP/data residency concessions)

Notes and references:
- Prototype modeling sheet: link to Confluence + spreadsheet (confluence:GTMPACK-874)
- Pilot deals to reference: JIRA PRO-1921 (Pilot with Drift)
- Please flag any language that causes friction in the field — iterate and keep the public-facing web copy simple and stable.

Open questions for leadership
- Do we want a public-facing page that lists exact token-to-price buckets, or keep public only 1–2 example lists and move details to quote?
- Should we pilot an aggressive volume discount (50%+ for large multi-year commits) for strategic logos, or ration that to a very small number of pre-approved enterprise plays?

Owner for execution:
- Growth PM (Priya Rao) to run starter pricing A/B
- Sales Ops (Leah Martinez) to implement discount approval flow in CRM
- Pricing committee to review final guardrails March quarter close

End of draft.

Action items:
- Collect feedback from AE cohort by 2026-03-10
- Finalize guardrails and publish approved snippets for web + sales by 2026-03-20
